However, in your main method, you're trying to create an instance of `Marks` using `student.new Marks(...)`. This syntax is used for **non-static** inner classes, where you need an instance of the outer class to create the inner class instance.
Since `Marks` is declared as `static`, it doesn't require an instance of the outer `Student` class to exist. Therefore, you should create it differently.
Student.Marks marks = student.new Marks(mark1, mark2, mark3);
Student.Marks marks = new Student.Marks(mark1, mark2, mark3);

This is the fundamental difference between static and non-static inner classes in Java. Static inner classes can be instantiated without an instance of the outer class, while non-static inner classes cannot.
